title: Eventual descent of finite-presentation flatness
statement: Let I be a directed set and let (S_i)_{i\in I} be an inverse system of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, where S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i) for Noetherian rings R_i, and let S=\varprojlim_i S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R). Fix i\in I, let X_i be a finitely presented S_i-scheme [def-pc-scheme], put X=X_i\times_{S_i}S and X_j=X_i\times_{S_i}S_j for j\ge i [def-pc-base-change], and let \mathcal{F}_i be a finitely presented quasi-coherent \mathcal{O}_{X_i}-module. If the pullback of \mathcal{F}_i to X is flat over S [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], then there is j\ge i such that the pullback of \mathcal{F}_i to X_{j'} is flat over S_{j'} for every j'\ge j.

source.place: Lemma 32.10.4, Tag 05LY, with Y_i=S_i (and for later stages since flatness is preserved by base change)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-flat-module-descent-affine-charts] to obtain finitely many rings B_b, modules N_b, and algebra maps a_b with the finite-presentation and flat limit tensor conditions, and a stage-flatness gluing implication. This carries out the finite-affine reduction and eventual-stage gluing in the original Tag 05LY proof.

source.place: Lemma 32.10.4, Tag 05LY, finite affine reduction, specialized to Y_i = S_i; Properties Tag 01PC; Morphisms Tag 01U4

proof.text: For each chart use [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-descent] on R and its chosen colimit cocone, taking A_i = R_i, B_i = B_b, N_i = N_b and the algebra map R_i -> B_b. The comparison supplies its flat limit hypothesis. This yields j_b >= i and flatness of its tensor module at every k >= j_b.

source.place: Tag 05LY, affine descent using Algebra Tag 02JO (3)

proof.text: Induct on a finite set of chart indices to find a common bound j >= i and j >= j_b for all its indices. For the empty set take i. For insertion, choose a directed upper bound of the previous bound and j_b and use transitivity. Apply this to Finset.univ. At any k >= j every chart is flat by the preceding step. Apply the stage gluing implication from Step 1 to obtain the required IsFlatOver. Proof irrelevance identifies the different proofs of i <= k in the displayed base-change morphisms.
